The same Lord Cardinal has already sent us, the day before yesterday, true copies of these letters, confirmed by his seal and sign and by the attestation of Richard Petterworth, public notary, to be published in our city and diocese in the manner and form described below, and carried out diligently and with all speed. The tenor of these apostolic letters follows word for word, and is as follows. Martin, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved son Henry, presbyter Cardinal of the title of St Eusebius, legate of the Apostolic See in all Germany and in the kingdoms of Hungary and Bohemia, greeting and apostolic blessing. The Saviour of all and Lord, for the redemption of the

units.la: gregis vt illum suæ hæreditatis participem faceret, in precifi immolari non abnuit, vices licet immeriti gerentes in terris circa eiusdem gregis, excubias vt in Saluatoris nostri exardeicens beneplacitis ad cœlestem gloriam euocetur, vigiliis, vacamus assiduis & prætermine reprobatorum & hæreticorum ad præcipiria quæq; trahentium insania discentis suæ malignitatis & perfutiæ laqueis in consutilem Dei tunicam quæ vnionem fidelium reprætentat, dilaniet & abscindat, sed vt illum Domino luctificaremus, alios vero deuiantes à Catholicis documentis peruerfissimos homines euertere atq; comprimere diuina nobis assistente gratia valeamus. Considerantes igitur iniquitatis alumnos Wicklefistas & Husitas, alioq; hæreticos & infideles qui verz salutis semitam deserentes Christianæ religionis persecutores acerrimos feferedunt, quiq; falsis & vesanis dogmatibus & damnatis erroribus, hæresiumq; fomentis Orthodoxam fidem euertere molientes vniuersum Regnū Bohemiæ & partes illi contermínas infecerunt, ac cupientes eorū temeritatem quantum cum Deo possumus obuiare, fideles milites Christi pugiles athletas visicæ crucis qua nos à damnatione redemit, caractere insignitos, cōtra præfatos hæreticos denuo duximus excitandos vt hæreticos ipsos qui Dei timore postpolito Ecclesias, monasteria, & alia pialoea Apostolorum, Martyrum, & confessorum sanguine dedicata, eorumq; imagines concrematât & euertant, ac fidem Catholicam in Germania & alibi confundere & delere moliuntur, a nequissimis eorum propositis quibus in Christianum lunguinem & Catholicos sacerdotes, sæpenumero debacchantur, non solum spiritualibus verum etiā temporalibus conuocatis præsidiis possimus authore Domino coercere. Hodie siquidem pro succedendis ex agro Dominico vepribus pestiferis ac nocisis, ac quibuslibet peruersis erroribus de ipsoru hæreticorū mentibus extirpandis, illorumq; salubri reductione ad gremium sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ paterna solicitudine vigilantes, vt quandoq; ad cor reuerti ab huiusmodi relipiscant erroribus, quibus gregem ipsum seducere & inficere moliuntur, & si forsan in eorum obstinatione perseuerare voluerint, euertantur.
units.tr: flock, that he might make it partakers of his inheritance, did not refuse to be offered as a precious sacrifice. We, though unworthy, bear his office on earth and keep watch over the same flock with constant vigils, so that, burning with zeal for our Saviour, we may be called to heavenly glory by his good pleasure. Our concern is that the madness of the reprobate and heretics, who drag many headlong into every ruin, may be restrained, so that they do not tear and cut apart, with the snares of their malice and perfidy, the seamless tunic of God which represents the unity of the faithful. We desire, with the divine grace assisting us, to restore the faithful to the Lord and to overthrow and suppress those who stray from Catholic teaching and are most perverse. Considering therefore the Wycliffites and Hussites, the nurslings of iniquity, and other heretics and unbelievers who, forsaking the path of true salvation, have become the most bitter persecutors of the Christian religion, and who, by false and frenzied doctrines, condemned errors and the fomenting of heresies, are striving to overthrow the Orthodox faith and have infected the whole kingdom of Bohemia and the neighbouring parts, and wishing, so far as we can with God's help, to check their rashness, we have decided to rouse again against the said heretics faithful soldiers of Christ, fighters and athletes marked with the sign of the cross by which he redeemed us from damnation. This is so that, with the help of the Lord, we may restrain those heretics who, having cast aside the fear of God, burn and overthrow churches, monasteries and other pious places dedicated by the blood of Apostles, Martyrs and Confessors, and their images, and who seek to confound and destroy the Catholic faith in Germany and elsewhere, and who rage against Christians and Catholic priests with their most wicked designs, not only by spiritual but also by temporal forces. For today, with paternal solicitude, we watch over the uprooting of pestilent and harmful brambles from the Lord's field, and the removal of every perverse error from the minds of these heretics, and their wholesome return to the bosom of holy Mother Church, so that at some time they may return to their senses and abandon the errors by which they strive to seduce and infect the flock; but if they should be pleased to persist in their obstinacy, let them be overthrown.

units.la: Te ad vniuersam Germaniam ac Hungariæ & Bohemiæ Regna tibi plenæ potestatis legati de latere officium committendo, de fratrum nostrorum consilio tanquam pacis Angelum prouidimus destinandum, prout in aliis nostris literis desuper confectis plenius continetur. Nos igitur cupientes vt huiusmodi legationis officium ad laudem & gloriam diuini nominis, ac salutem & pacem fidelium animarum eò facilius exequaris, quò amplioni fueris authoritate imbutus, directisin cœlum oculis ad illum cuius res agitur, diuinum & humanum præsidium inuocantes, vt huiusmodi adiuti præsidiis, eorundem hæreticorum temeritatem, filii se ad Christum conuerterint, coercere & comprimere valeamus, charissimos in Christo filios nostros Reges, ac dilectos filios Duces, Marchiones, Principes, Barones, Comites, Capitaneos, Magistratus, & quoslibet alios officiales, eorumq; loca tenentes, communitates quoq; & Vniuersitates, ciuitatum, terrarum, oppidorum, castrorum, villarum, & aliorum quorumcunq; locorum, cæterorumq; Christiani nominis zelotes, statūs dignitatis, & religionis cuiuslibet, vbilibet per Angliam, & in locis quibuslibet constitutos rogamus, requirimus, & hortamur, ac per aspersionem sanguinis omnium gloriosissimi Redemptoris paternis affectibus obsectamus, in fuorū remissionem peccaminum, eis suadentes, vt ad Wicklefistarum, Husfistarum, & aliorum hæreticorum præfatorum insurrectionem & exterminium, ac ad impendendum tibi contra eos profutura suffragia, quibus tam salutaris negotii persecutio adiuuetur potenter, atq; viriliter se accingant, quos spiritualibus donis indulgentiis videlicet & peccatorum suorum remissionibus de ipsorum fratrū consilio prouidimus mittendos Quocirca circumspectioni tuæ per Apostolica scripta committimus, & mandamus, quatenus tu per te vel venerabiles fratres nostros Patriarchas, Archiepiscopos, & Episcopos, ac dilectos filios, electos, administratores, Abbates, priores, aliosq; Ecclesiarū & monasteriorū Prælatos, & cæteros Christianæ religionis professores, vbilibet per Germaniam & alibi residentes, quos tibi in coadiutores super his duxeris eligendos, quos perce vel deputandos à te contra hæreticos ipsos, exercitum conuocari, vel expeditionem aut quamuis aliam ordinationem fieri contigerit, ad præmissum tam salutare negotium perquendū, velut præconnes fortes exaltādo in ipso crucis nomine voces vestras in singulis ciuitatibus & diocesibus, terris, castris, villis, & locis Angliæ quibuslibet, vbi congruè profexeris, vel profexerint iuxta datam tibi & illis à Deo prudentiam, quibusunq; Christi fidelibus ad id audiendum confluentibus, quibus vero pœnitentibus & confessis vt ad idlibertius inducātur, verbum salutiferæ crucis ac ipsius admirabile signum publicè proponere & prædicare procures, at ipsi Patriarchæ, Archiepiscopi, Episcopi, electi, administratores, Abbates, & alii quos elegeris, Catholici sacerdotes studeant & procurent, illudq; fidelibus ipsis id devoté suscipere volentibus tuis ac ipsorum eligendorum exhortationibus ac opportunis monitionibus ptæuiis, vt cum debita Reuerentia tam gloriosum signum recipiant, idq; contra peruersa molimina, & conatus eorundem hæreticoram sniscordibus imprimatur, & negociorum huiusmodi fidelibus & seruentibus animus persequantur, eadem authoritate concedas, & ipsi eligendi concedant, eorumq; humeris affigat pariter & affigatur.
units.tr: Having appointed you, with the full power of a legate a latere, to the office of legate in all Germany and the kingdoms of Hungary and Bohemia, we have, with the counsel of our brethren, provided that you be sent as an angel of peace, as is more fully contained in our other letters on this matter. We therefore, desiring that you may the more easily carry out the office of this legation, to the praise and glory of the divine name and the salvation and peace of the faithful souls, and that, the more amply you are endowed with authority, the more directing your eyes to heaven, and invoking divine and human aid from him whose cause it is, you may be able, aided by such help, to restrain and suppress the rashness of those heretics, until they are converted to Christ, we ask, exhort and urge our most dear sons in Christ the Kings, and our beloved sons the Dukes, Marquises, Princes, Barons, Earls, Captains, magistrates and any other officials and their deputies, and also the communities and universities of cities, lands, towns, fortresses, villages and other places whatever, and all other zealots of the Christian name, of whatever rank, dignity or religion, established wherever in England and in any places, and we beseech them, by the blood of the most glorious Redeemer, with paternal affection, for the remission of their sins, persuading them that, for the uprising and extermination of the aforesaid Wycliffites, Hussites and other heretics, and for the furnishing of aid to you against them, which will powerfully and manfully support the pursuit of so salutary a business, they gird themselves; whom, with spiritual gifts, namely indulgences and remissions of their sins, we have provided, with the counsel of our brethren, to be sent. Wherefore we commit and command to your circumspection by these apostolic writings that you, either in person or through our venerable brethren the Patriarchs, Archbishops and Bishops, and our beloved sons, the elect, administrators, Abbots, priors and other prelates of churches and monasteries, and the other professors of the Christian religion, wherever they reside throughout Germany and elsewhere, whom you shall choose as your co-workers in these matters, or whom you shall appoint or depute, should it happen that an army is raised against those heretics, or an expedition or any other arrangement is made, to pursue this so salutary business, as strong heralds, raising your voices in the name of the cross in individual cities and dioceses, lands, fortresses, villages and places of England, wherever you or they shall appropriately go, according to the prudence given to you and them by God, and to all faithful of Christ who gather to hear it, and that you take care to proclaim and preach publicly the word of the saving cross and its wonderful sign, so that the penitent and confessed may be more freely induced to take it up; and that the said Patriarchs, Archbishops, Bishops, elect, administrators, Abbots, and others whom you choose, as Catholic priests, take care and see to it that the sign is received with due reverence by the faithful who are willing to take it devoutly, through your exhortations and those of the men you choose, and through opportune admonitions, so that it may be imprinted on them as a sign against the perverse designs and attempts of these heretics, and so that the faithful and fervent pursue this kind of business, you grant the same authority, and the chosen ones are to grant it likewise, and it is to be affixed to their shoulders.

units.la: Nosenim ab intimis nostris præcordiis affectantes vt toti orbi innotescant, quanta meritis nostræ amaritudine sustinemus contra gregem Christi talia perpetrantes, tantifque insolentiis & facinoribus quantum cum Deo possumus obuiantes, & vt fideles ipsi ad id eo feruentius animentur, quo veriorem gratiam exinde se nouerint perceptueros, de Omnipotentis Dei misericordia, & beatorum Petri & Pauli Apostolorum eius authoritate confisi, & illa quam dedit nobis Deus ligandi atq; soluendi potestatem, eisdem fi- delibus qui crucis eiusdem signo suscepto per illud tempus quod per te vel alium in huiusmodi prædicatione eis duxeris præsigendum, & quoties pro extirpatione hæresium ad te veniendo, vel quo fideles ipsos contra eosdem hæreticos accedendo transmiseris, contra illos prefato exercitui in personis propriis interfuerint, & expensis quilibet vt interbi interessent, sine fraude iter arripuerint, si in ipso fuerint itinere vita functi, plena suorum peccaminum, de quibus corde contriti & ore confessi fuerint, veniam impertimur, & in retributionem iustorum salutis æternæ pollicemur augmentum eis, quod qui non in personis propriis illuc accesserint, sed ipsorum dumtaxat expensis iuxta suarum facultatum qualitatem & exigentiam, idoneos destinauerint bellatores, ac illis licet alienis expensis, propriis tamen adiecerint, in personis plenam suorum concedimus veniam peccatorum.
units.tr: For, desiring from the depths of our hearts that it may become known to the whole world how great bitterness we bear, on account of the merits of those who perpetrate such things against the flock of Christ, and resisting, so far as we can with God, such insolences and crimes, and that the faithful may be the more fervently encouraged, knowing that they will receive from it a truer grace, trusting in the mercy of Almighty God and the authority of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and by the power of binding and loosing which God gave us, we grant full remission of their sins, of which they are contrite in heart and have confessed with their mouth, to those faithful who have taken the sign of the cross and who, within the time that you or another shall appoint for this preaching, and as often as they come to you, or you send them to go against those heretics for the uprooting of heresies, have taken part in person in that army against them, and who, that they might take part, have set out on the journey without fraud at their own expense, and if they have died on the journey. We promise, moreover, as a reward of the just, an increase of eternal salvation. Those who have not gone in person but have sent suitable fighters at their own expense, in proportion to their means and need, and have added their own to what others provided, even at another's expense, we grant full remission of sins as if in person.

units.la: Cæterum vero qui in personis propriis interesse & propter inopiam suis expensis alios destinare nequiuerint, dummodo huiusmodi durante persecutione negocii in ieiuniis & orationibus perseuerent, supplicitèr exorando quod altissimus dignetur ipsos fideles de peruersis hæreticis victoriam reportare, sexaginta dies de iniunctis eis pœnitentiis misericord iter relaxamus, huiusmodi quoq; remissionis volumus & concedimus esse participes iuxta quantutate subsidii & deuotionis affectum, eos omnes qui durantibus expeditione & exercitu supradictis, pro huiusmodi consummatione negocii congrue ministrauerint & circa illud auxilium & consilii impenderint opportunæ, vniuersos prætereaa & singulos quos eodem signo crucis munire contigerit (vt præsertur) illo priuilegio illa; immunitate gaudere decernimus, quæcruce signatis pro tertæ sanctæ, subsidio in generali Concilio sunt concessa, eorumq; personas, nec non familiâ, res, & bona, sub beati Petri & Apostolicæ sedis atq; nostra protectione permanere debere. Statuentes iosuper vt bona prædicta extunc, donec de eorum reditu vel obitu certissime constiterit integra maneant & quieta. Illorû vero Archiepiscopi, nec non Archidiaconi, & aliisuperiores, eorumq; officiales, ipsos ac huiusmodi bona authoritate prædicta tueantur, nő permittedo eos contra huiusmodi statuti tenorê ab aliquibus indebite molestari: molestatores & contradictores quoslibet & rebelles per censurâ Ecclesiasticâ & alia iuris remedia, appellatione postposita compescendo, inuocando etiâ ad hoc si opus fuerit auxilium brachii secularis, non obstante si aliquibus comuniter vel dilam in sede indultum, q; interdici, suspendi, vel excommunicari non possent per literas Apostolicas, non sacientes plenâ & expressam, ac de verbo ad verbum de indulto huiusmodi monitionem. Cæterû vt ipsius viuificæ crucis signo muniti, eò facilius reddantur huiusmodi remissionû & indulgentiarû participes, quo se liberius eximere posse conspexerint ab onere delictorû, tibi & eisdem Patriarchis, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis, electis, Abbatibus, & Prælatis, ac aliis idoneis sacerdotib. secularibus, vel regularibus, ad id per te assumendis, de quibus tibi pro tempore visum fuerit, vt tu & ipsi omnium pro huiusmodi negocii expeditione consignatorum confiteri volentium, confessiones audire, ipsisq; confessionibus diligenter auditis pro peccatis suis & excessibus omnibus per illos comissis, etiâ si ex manuum iniectione in Clericos & religiosos, aut incendiarii vel sacrilegi fuerint, debita: ac solutionis beneficiû impendere, & iniungere pœnitentiâ salutarem, etiamsi huiusmodi peccata tâ grandia & enormia essent, propter q dicta sedes esset merito cõsulta, liberè & licite valeas authoritate pdicta tenore præsentium indulgemus. Verû quia difficile videretut præsentes literas sigillis exhiberi, volumus quod tu huiusmodi literarû transumptum, propria manu confectum, tuoq; sigillo immunitati impendenti iniunctum, personis & locis singulis, vbi & quod tibi expedire videbitur, transmitti & insinuari procures. Cui quidem transumpto
units.tr: Furthermore, as for those who cannot themselves take part in person and, through poverty, are unable to send others at their own expense: provided that, while this business of the campaign lasts, they persevere in fasting and prayer, earnestly beseeching Almighty God to grant to the faithful victory over the perverse heretics, we mercifully relax sixty days of the penances enjoined on them. We wish and grant that all who, while the aforesaid expedition and army last, shall suitably minister to the accomplishment of this business, and shall contribute appropriate help and counsel toward it, shall share in this remission, in proportion to the measure of their aid and the warmth of their devotion. Moreover, we decree that all and each of those whom the sign of the cross shall have been placed upon (as is said) enjoy that privilege and immunity which were granted by the General Council to those signed with the cross for the aid of the Holy Land; and that their persons, as well as their households, goods and property, remain under the protection of the blessed Peter, of the Apostolic See and of ourselves. We further ordain that the said goods remain whole and undisturbed until their return or death is most certainly known. The archbishops, archdeacons and other superiors of these men, and their officials, are to defend them and these goods by the aforesaid authority, not permitting them to be unjustly harassed by anyone contrary to the tenor of this statute. Any troublers, opponents and rebels are to be restrained by ecclesiastical censure and other legal remedies, without appeal, invoking for this purpose, if need be, the help of the secular arm; notwithstanding whatever indults may have been granted to any persons, commonly or by name, that they cannot be interdicted, suspended or excommunicated by Apostolic letters unless these contain full and express mention, word for word, of such an indult. Moreover, so that those marked with the sign of the life-giving cross may more easily become sharers in these remissions and indulgences, and may see themselves more freely released from the burden of their sins, we grant to you, and to the same Patriarchs, Archbishops, Bishops, elect, Abbots and Prelates, and to other suitable priests, secular or regular, whom you may appoint for this purpose and whom you think fit, that you and they may hear the confessions of all the signed who wish to confess for this business's accomplishment. Having diligently heard these confessions, you may freely and lawfully, by the aforesaid authority and by the tenor of these present letters, impose a salutary penance and grant absolution for their sins and all the excesses committed by them, even if they have laid violent hands on clerics or religious, or are arsonists or sacrilegious persons, and even if these sins were so grave and enormous that the said See would rightly have to be consulted. But because it would be difficult to exhibit the present letters under seal, we wish that you procure a copy of these letters, made by your own hand and sealed with your seal, to be sent and made known to individual persons and places, where and as it shall seem fitting to you.

units.la: r tránsumpto velut ótiganalibus literis vbiq; dare volumus & decernimus plenam fidem. Datę Romæ apud sanctos Apostolicos. 15. Kal. Aprilis, pontificatus nostri anno decimo.
units.tr: To this copy, as to the original letters, we wish and decree that full faith be given everywhere. Given at Rome, at the Holy Apostles, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the tenth year of our pontificate.

units.la: Nos igitur, Henricus Archiepiscopus antedictus volentes præfatas literas apostolicas, & singula in eis contenta, quatenus nos ciuitatem q; nostrã & diocesin concernunt, authoritate Apostolica per dictum Dominum Cardinalem nobis commissa publicare, & renerenter exequi, vt tenemur, vobis cõiunctim & diuisim cõmittimus & mãdamus, in virtute sanctæ obedientiæ firmiter ininngendo, quatenus literas ipsas Apostolicas, & plenum effectum earundē in Ecclesia nostra eathedrali, villisq; & locis aliis nostrę diocesis, ac in synodis & capitulis, clericisq; congregationibus, coram Clero & populo specialiter ad hoc vocatis clare, distinctè, & aperte in vulgari cum exhortationibus devotis, & inductionibus diebus sestiuis & dominicis receptione vestram præsentium proximè immediate sequentib. publicetis, & sic faciatis ab aliis publicari. Intimantes eisdē Clero & populo, ac Christi fidelibus nostrę diocesis quibuscunq;, quod nos authoritate Apostolica (vt pferetur) cõmissa certos ordinauimus & deputauimus (prout tenore præsentiū ordinamus & deputamus) prędicatores & confessores in locis diuersis nostrę diocesis, videlicet dilectos in Christo filios fratres Iacobum Groue & Thomam Ashe, Monachos Ecclesiæ nostrę Cantuariæ in Ecclesia, & ciuitate nostra Cantuariæ fratrem Iohannem Wotton priorem Douerię apud Donert, Magistrum Mattheum Ashton legum doctorem apud Wingham, Magnum Thomam Moome in decretis licentiam apud Deie & Sandwicum, & illas partes, & magistros Iohannem Gorfich baccalaureum in Theologia, vicarium Ecclesiæ de Wrotham, ac Iohannem Botle in legibus baccalaureum apud Maydeston, & in illis partibus, Magistrum Iohannę Warreue legum doctorē Rectorem Ecclesię beatę Mariæ in Marisco & Romeney, ac Magistrum Walterum Adam in legibus baccalaureū Rectorem Ecclesiæ paroch ialis de Aldington, & Dominum Wilhelmū Loue Vicarium de Lyde ibidē & pro partibus illis, qnos ad hoc tàm in munere sufficientes quàm in scientia idoneos pro populo nostrę diocesis reputamus, qui etiam prædicatores verbum crucis salutiferæ & ipsius admirabile signum cunctis Christi fidelibus infinuabunt, proponent, & publicè prędicabunt, ipsorumque confessiones audient, eosque à peccatis seorum absoluent, & signum sanctæ crucis huiusmodi omnibus & singulis suscipere volentibus concedent, & ipsorum humeris affigent, iuxta & secundum formam & effectum informationum, instructionum, & articulorum præsatı Domini Cardinalis, diuisim (vt præfertur) autoritate (quą supra) plenam committimus in domino potestatem, Absolutionibus tumomnium & singulorum cruce signatorum in casibus grauibus, propter quos sedes Apostolica foret consulenda, præfato Domino Cardinali speciliter reseruatis.
units.tr: Therefore we, the aforesaid Henry, Archbishop, wishing that the aforesaid apostolic letters, and each thing contained in them, insofar as they concern us, our city and our diocese, be published by the authority apostolic committed to us by the said Lord Cardinal, and be reverently carried out as we are bound to do, commit and command to you, jointly and severally, enjoining it firmly in virtue of holy obedience: that you publish the same apostolic letters, and their full effect, clearly, distinctly and openly in the vernacular, in our cathedral church, in the villages and other places of our diocese, and in synods and chapters and assemblies of clergy, before the clergy and people specially called to this, with devout exhortations and inducements, on the festival days and Sundays immediately following the receipt of these present letters; and that you so cause them to be published by others. Making known to the same clergy and people, and to all the faithful of our diocese whomsoever, that by the apostolic authority committed to us (as is said) we have ordained and appointed (as by the tenor of these present we do ordain and appoint) preachers and confessors in various places of our diocese, namely our beloved sons in Christ, the brothers James Grove and Thomas Ashe, monks of our church of Canterbury, in the church and city of Canterbury; Brother John Wotton, prior of Dover, at Dover; Master Matthew Ashton, doctor of laws, at Wingham; Master Thomas Moome, licentiate in decretals, at Deal and Sandwich and those parts; and Master John Gorfich, bachelor of theology, vicar of the church of Wrotham; and John Botle, bachelor of laws, at Maidstone and in those parts; Master John Warreue, doctor of laws, rector of the church of St Mary in the Marsh and Romney; and Master Walter Adam, bachelor of laws, rector of the parish church of Aldington; and Sir William Loue, vicar of Lyde there, and for those parts; whom we consider sufficient both in office and learned in knowledge for the people of our diocese. These preachers will also make known and publicly proclaim to all the faithful of Christ the word of the saving cross and its wonderful sign; they will hear their confessions, absolve them from their sins, and grant the sign of the holy cross to all and each who wish to receive it, and affix it to their shoulders, according to the form and effect of the information, instructions and articles of the aforesaid Lord Cardinal. We commit to them, separately (as is said), by the authority (as above), full power in the Lord, including absolutions of all and each of those signed with the cross in grave cases, for which the Apostolic See would have to be consulted, these cases being specially reserved to the aforesaid Lord Cardinal.

units.la: Volumus insuper, & authoritate supradicta mandamus, quòd singuli prædicatores & confessores superius nominati & deputati in vestris manibus corporaliter præstentiramenta, quod ipsi quæ sibi committuntur in præmissis iustè, bene, & fideliter exequentur, iuxta & secundum Insormationes & instructiones superius memoratas. Siquì verò fuerint qui huiusmodi sanctæ crucis signum a nobis affectent recipere, ad nostram accedant præsentiam, qui semper parati erimus per Dei graciam in persona propria cum totius animi deuotione notum id eis, quod nobis authoritate sua supra committitur impertiri.
units.tr: We further wish, and by the aforesaid authority command, that each of the preachers and confessors named above and appointed shall swear bodily in your hands that they will carry out justly, well and faithfully what is committed to them in the foregoing matters, according to the information and instructions mentioned above. If there be any who desire to receive this sign of the holy cross from us, let them come into our presence, for we shall always be ready, by the grace of God, in our own person, with all devotion of mind, to impart to them what has been committed to us by that authority.

units.la: Dictis insuper prædicatoribus & confessoribus nostra pro parte vobis exponere mandamus, quòd ipsorum singuli, nomina singulorum per ipsos & eorum quemlibet cruce signandorum redigit faciant in scripturam. Moneantetiam iidem prædicatores & confessores cruce signatos huiusmodi quoscunq;, quod ante vel post ipsam susceptam crucem ad præsentiam præsati Domini Cardinalis vbicunq; sue-rit, ad vltimum citra primùm diem mensis Marcii proximè futuri personaliter accedant, andituri ab ipso & scituri quid vlterius in diċtæ crucis negocio fuerit faciēdum. Et quid feceritis in præmissis noscitra vicęsimum diem mensis Februarii proximè futuri debite, distinctè, & aperte certificetis per vestras, & sic certificetur vtrumque vestrum per suas literas patentes harum seriem ac nomina, & cognomina cruce signatorum huiusmodi, quæ vos à prædicatoribus & confessoribus prædictis recipere volumus, in schedula litteris vestris certificatoriis annexenda, descripta continentes autenticè sigillatis. Datę in munerio nostro de Slyndon, primo die mensis Ianuarii. Anno Do. 1428. & nostrę translationis Anno. 15.
units.tr: Moreover, we command you to set forth on our behalf to the said preachers and confessors that each of them is to have the names of each person signed with the cross, by them or any of them, written down in a record. The same preachers and confessors are also to admonish all those so signed, whether before or after they have taken up the cross, that they must present themselves in person before the presence of the said Lord Cardinal, wherever he may be, no later than the first day of next March, to hear from him and learn what further is to be done in the business of the said cross. And you are to certify duly, distinctly and openly, by your letters, what you have done in the foregoing matters, no later than the twentieth day of next February; and each of you is to certify to the other by his letters patent, authentically sealed, containing the tenor and the names and surnames of the signed persons whom you wish to receive from the aforesaid preachers and confessors, written out on a schedule to be annexed to your letters of certification. Given at our manor of Slindon, on the first day of January, in the year of Our Lord 1428, and in the fifteenth year of our translation.

units.la: Hoc anno Henricus Archiepiscopus à Papa Martino quinto Caudinalis Romanus titulo præsbyteri sancti Eusebii, & eiusdem in Anglia Legatus creatus est. Verùm ne auctoritatem illam legatianam sine Regis permissu ac licentia, contra iura & consuetudines regni feceret, Richardus quidam Candray Clericus Regis procurator constitutus est, ut ab omnibus iniuriis, grauaminibus & præiudiciis per Papam aut Romanam curiam in Regem, atq; regnum illar̄ seu inferendis ad proximum generale Concilium provocaret, Itaq; simulatq; compertum est Archiepiscopum legatinam potestatem irrequisito Rege suscepisse & legationis insignia tulisse, Richardus Candray procurator Regius coram Humfrido Glocestriæ Duce Regis minoris curatore, & Ehenii, Bathoniensi, atq; Norwicensi Episcopis, nec non Staffordiæ & Huntingdoniæ Comitibus, & Walter o Hungerford Thesaurario, ac Radulpho Cromwell Baronne Regiis Cōsiliariis præsentibus appellationem ab eo atq; à Papa ad Concilium in scriptis interposuit. In qua expressit, quòd nullus Apostolicæ sedis legatus venire debeat in regnum Regis Angliæ, aut alias suas terras & dominia nisi ad Regis Angliæ ,p ιcpote existentis vocationem, petitionem, requisitionem, seu rogatum, Romanis pontificibus tolerantibus & consentientibus tamen tacitè quàm expressè. In quatamen appellatione si dictus Archiepiscopus non tanquam legatus, sibi liceret. In quibus Rex eatenus ei subuenirèt, quatenus id iuribus & priuilegiis suæ Regiæ coronæ, atq; inelyti sui Angliæ Regni facere posset. Hac appellatione exscripto recitata Archiepiscopus in præsentia prætatorum præsulum atq; procerum fassus & protestatus est.
units.tr: In this year Archbishop Henry was created a Roman cardinal by Pope Martin V, with the title of priest of St Eusebius, and legate of the same in England. But lest he should exercise that legatine authority without the king's permission and leave, contrary to the laws and customs of the realm, one Richard Candray, the king's clerk, was appointed proctor, to appeal to the next general council against all the injuries, grievances and prejudices which the pope or the Roman curia might inflict on the king and the realm. So as soon as it was discovered that the archbishop had assumed legatine power without the king's request and had borne the insignia of a legate, Richard Candray, the king's proctor, in the presence of Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, the king's guardian during his minority, the bishops of Ely, Bath and Norwich, the earls of Stafford and Huntingdon, Walter Hungerford the treasurer, and Ralph Cromwell, Baron, the king's councillors, lodged in writing an appeal against him and against the pope to the council. In it he declared that no legate of the apostolic see ought to come into the kingdom of England, or into the king's other lands and dominions, unless summoned, petitioned, requested or invited by the king of England for the time being, the Roman pontiffs tolerating and consenting, though tacitly rather than expressly. And in this appeal it was stated that, if the said archbishop were allowed to act not as legate, the king would assist him so far as he could do so consistently with the rights and privileges of his royal crown and of his renowned kingdom of England. This appeal, having been copied out and read aloud, the archbishop, in the presence of the aforesaid prelates and nobles, acknowledged and protested.

units.la: Quod non fuit, nec est, neq; etit suæ intentionis per ingressum suum in Angliam, neq; per aliquid per eum facta seu facienda, dicta seu dicenda legatinam potestatem quam suscepērat sine permissu Regio exercere, nec iuribus, priuilegiis, libertatibus, aut consuetudinibus Regis atque Regni in aliquo derogare, aut contrauenire, id eadem omnia & singula conseruare, defendere, manutenere, atq; robotare.
units.tr: That it was not, is not, and will not be his intention, by his entry into England, or by anything done, to be done, said or to be said by him, to exercise the legatine power he had received without royal permission, nor in any respect to derogate from or contravene the rights, privileges, liberties or customs of the king and the kingdom; and that he would preserve, defend, maintain and uphold all and each of these same things.

units.la: Superior synodus sex amplius mensibus dufauit, in eaque magna contra Wiclyffianos statuta persecutio fuit, ab Wilhelmo Lynwood officiali curiæ Cant. de Arcubus, Thomaꞓ Bronwe vicario Areh generali, atq; Thoma Beckingtō Decano de Arcubus, certa quæda via: iurificâ formula descripta, quaīn Wiclyfianos & hæreticos fuerit procedendum. Hoc anno qui fuit octauus Regni Henrici sexti in Parlamento statutum est, ut prælatì atq; clerici eorum, familatus cum ad synodos accesserint, iidem priuilegiis acimmunitatibus gaudeant, quibus milites & Burgenses Parlamenti. Interhanc autem & ea quentem proximam synodum quatuor pene annis in eredi fuerit: Quæ causa Basiliensis Concilii congregatio est. Nam Eugenius Papa Concilium hoc authoritate papali dimisit. Sed Cardinales & Prælati coniuncti concilium adhuc inutilo Papa celebrarunt. Synodus itaq; decreuit, ut ad Papam legari, & ad Concilium procuratores docti ac facundi mitterentur, ad quorū sumptus sustinēdos ex singulis libris duo denarii à Clero concessi sunt. Tum Iohannes Stafford Episcopus Bathoniensis Cancellarius, & D. Scroope the saurarius Regni, nec non Wilhelmus Lyndewood Custos priuatigilli pro Rege lubsidiō pestularunt, & mediam decimam tandem ægrè impetrarunt. In hac synodo multa contra Episcopos ab inferioribus prælatis querelæ delatæ sunt, quòd Vicarios generales, Officiales, atq; Commissarios ignaros & imperitos legum in diocesibus suis statuerunt. Constitutum itaq̄ est ne quis iuris dictionem Ecclesiasticam exercerēt, nisi iuris Ciuilis aut Canonici gradum aliquem à Cantebrigiēli vel Oxoniensi Academia accepisset. Ac proxime etiam anno cum legatis, nuncii ad Papam & Basiliense Concilium (vt diximus) missi rediissent, synodus iterum Londini conuncit, in qua deliberatum est, virum Eugenium Papam, an Concilium Basiliense sequerentur. In qua deliberatione inferior synodus decreuit Concilio deferto esse Papæ adhærendum, Cui decreto ab Episcopis etiam assensum est. In hac synodo postulatum pro Rege decimam Clerus denegauit, verum instantibus magna contentione procerib⁹ tandem concessit. In proxima verò synodo ferucnti petitę nihil actum est, præter diem festum Fridiwidæ inter sanctas relatæ decretum. Verum postquam illa longa inter Concilium & Eugenium Papam controuersia, siquidem transfacta fuerat, Eugenius Concilium à Basilea auocauit, & ad Ferrariam Italiæ ciuitatem transtulit. Igitur Archiepiscopus synodo Londinum conuocata cum Episcopis & prælatis de procuratoribus ac Legatis ad Concilium mittendis, eorumq; sumptibus egit. Sed inferiores prælati quia Episcopi tantum & Abbates generalibus Concilijs interesse consueuerunt, non esse sibi eiusmodi sumptuum onus imponendum aiunt, neque quicquam præstiterunt. Itaque ab Episcopis & Abbatibus ex singulis libris quatuor denarii legatis profeêturis tributi sunt. Ad hanc synodum Eugenius Papa more pontificio literas humanita& shy;te atque odio permixtas dedit, in quibus declarauit Elienfium Episcopatum simulatque vacaret Lodouico Rhotomagensi Archiepiscopo commendationis titulo sese contulisse. Fuit tum Philippus Motgan senex egregie cordatus Episcopus Elienfis ordine vice­simus tertius, qui vitam in senectute tam diuturnam produxit vt Papa commendationem quam totaiuñe synodus exercitaret, more Lodouici quiante eum obiit irritam fruitra ret. Hanc autem synodum alia proximo anno sequuta est, in qua sine mora & difficultate concessa fuit Regi decima, atq; omnia Cleri adiumenta vberrime promissa, issiliasduras Prematuræ leges quibus sapissime falsò accusarentur, ac quibus Clerus tanquam infi& shy;quis laqueis irretiti tenerentur, abrogaret. Rex iam in minore ætate constitutus, (nondum enim decimum nonum annum attigerat) se eum ad legitimam ætatem peruenire curaturum ne Clerus tam duris legibus & actionibus vrgeatur benignè respondit. Interim enim leges antea latas commodè nouari non posse. Atque hæc quidem vltima fuit ab hoc Archiepiscopo celebrata synodus, de quo etli tres deinde annos vixerat, tamen nona deo multa praeter ea quæ ipse ad memoriam sui nominis perennem fecit, dicenda supersunt. Vitum prudentem & magnanimum fuisse constat, & si illa papalis suffrimo abfuiistet quæ fuit tum cotagione omnes per quæ gentes infecit, de Ecclesia perinde acde Rep. optime meritum. Huic Archiepiscopo Wilhelmus Lynwood constitutiones Archiepi& shy;scopales a se in pulchrum consonantium digestas, & accuratissimis commentariis explicatas dedicauit. Wilhelmus autem Lynwood primò fuit officialis curiæ de Arcubus, de­indecustos priuati sigilli regii, ac demum ad Mencuensem Episc. eueduus. Idem Arch. in oppido de Heigham Ferreys in quo(vt diximus) natus est, Collegium magnificè extruxit, in quoClericos seculares, & præbendarios beneficiis & dignitatibus Ecclesiasticis lo­cupletatos collocauit. Ac in eodem oppido pauperibus holpitalem dom ũ condidit, eiq; multa prædia in vsum & eleemosynas pauperum comparauit, quòd a fratribus deinde suis Roberto & Wilhelmo Chicheley ciuibus Londinensibus quos in testamento hæredes instituit, permultis aliis adiectis & acquisitis prædiis auctum & dilatatum est. Neque his extrudis Archiepiscopus acquiuit, quin Oxonii ad literarum studia culenda colle­gium eelcberrimum omnium animarum, nec non Collegium Sancti Bernardi quod postea a Thoma Whit Maiore Londinensi & Militæ possessionibus auctum, & Collegi­um S. Iohannis appellatum est erexit. Cantuariæ præterea bibliothecam reparauit, ac euiusq; generis librisin structuit, maximam Campanis partem fabricauit, ac Conuen­tui plurimo ornamenta ac iocalia dedit. Viuus proprium tumulum in qua sepeliendus etat mortuus. Conuentus consensu in Ecclesia Cantuariensi condidit. Procuratores curiæ suæ de Arcubus iudice sedete eo indui habitu quo in Academiis artium Bacchalaurei vruntur primusiussit. In iurisdictione exercenda seueritatem cum æquitate coniun­xit, ac nesummis quidem eum deliquissent pepercit, Nam Dominus Strange, & Iohan& shy;nes Truffel Miles hostiliter inuicem affecti eum ad Dunstanii orientalis templum Lon& shy;dini in festo Parasceues obuii essent, pugnam eum suis famulis & clientibus commisi­runt. In ea pugna & conflictatione eum in Ecclesiâ itruissent Thomam Petwarden eiusdem parochiæ ciuem Londinensem interemerunt. Itaque Archiepiscopus exde iam facta, & sanguine Christiano in Ecclesia fuso omnes qui eam pugnam commisebant, & in Ecclesiam irruebant excommunicauit. Posteaq; de primisillius constitutionis autho­ribus inquisiuit, & cum comperisset D. Strange, & eius vxorem causam primam dedisse tanto tumultui, eos nominatim ad crucem Paulinam proximo die dominico excommunicatos denunciari præcepit. Qui deinde ad eum flexis genibus supplices ve& shy;nerunt, & absolui multis precibus petierunt. His Archiepiscopus hanc poenitentiam iniunxit.
units.tr: The previous synod lasted more than six months, and in it a great persecution was decreed against the Wycliffites, by William Lyndwood, official of the Court of Arches of Canterbury, Thomas Brown, vicar-general, and Thomas Beckington, dean of the Arches, who drew up a certain way and legal formula by which the Wycliffites and heretics were to be proceeded against. In this year, which was the eighth of the reign of Henry VI, it was enacted in Parliament that prelates and clergy, with their households, when they came to synods, should enjoy the same privileges and immunities as the knights and burgesses of Parliament. Nearly four years passed between this synod and the next, and the reason was the assembly of the Council of Basel. For Pope Eugenius had dissolved that council by papal authority; but the cardinals and prelates, joined together, still held the council without the pope. The synod therefore decreed that legates be sent to the pope, and learned and eloquent proctors to the council, and for the sustaining of their expenses the clergy granted two pence from each pound. Then John Stafford, bishop of Bath, the chancellor, Lord Scrope, treasurer of the realm, and William Lyndwood, keeper of the privy seal, petitioned on behalf of the king for a subsidy, and at last with difficulty obtained a half-tenth. In this synod the lesser prelates brought many complaints against the bishops, that in their dioceses they had appointed vicars-general, officials and commissaries who were ignorant and inexperienced in the laws. It was therefore decreed that no one should exercise ecclesiastical jurisdiction unless he had received some degree in civil or canon law from the university of Cambridge or Oxford. And in the following year, when the legates and messengers sent to the pope and to the Council of Basel (as we have said) had returned, the synod met again at London, in which it was debated whether they should follow Pope Eugenius or the Council of Basel. In this debate the lower synod decreed that, the council being abandoned, they should adhere to the pope; the bishops also assented to this decree. In this synod the clergy refused the tenth requested for the king, but at last, under great pressure from the nobles, granted it. In the next synod, although the request was earnestly pressed, nothing was accomplished, except a decree that the feast of St Frideswide be listed among the saints' days. But after that long controversy between the council and Pope Eugenius had been settled, Eugenius recalled the council from Basel and transferred it to the Italian city of Ferrara. The archbishop therefore called a synod to London, and with the bishops and prelates dealt with the proctors and legates to be sent to the council, and with their expenses. But the lesser prelates say that, since only bishops and abbots are accustomed to attend general councils, such a burden of expense should not be laid on them, and they contributed nothing. So from the bishops and abbots four pence from each pound were paid to the legates about to set out. To this synod Pope Eugenius, in the papal manner, sent letters mingled with courtesy and ill will, in which he declared that he had bestowed the see of Ely, as soon as it should fall vacant, on Louis, archbishop of Rouen, by way of a commendam. At that time Philip Morgan, an old and eminently wise bishop of Ely, the twenty-third in order, was living, and he prolonged his life into old age so far that the pope's commendation, which the whole synod had opposed, came to nothing, since Louis died before him. This synod was followed the next year by another, in which, without delay or difficulty, a tenth was granted to the king, and all aid from the clergy was most abundantly promised, on condition that he would repeal those harsh praemunire laws by which the clergy were very often falsely accused and held entangled as in unjust snares. The king, though still a minor (for he had not yet reached his nineteenth year), kindly replied that he would take care, when he came of legal age, that the clergy should not be pressed by such harsh laws and actions; for in the meantime the laws previously enacted could not conveniently be altered. This was the last synod held under this archbishop, and although he lived three more years, many things remain to be said of him besides those which he did to make his name lasting in memory. It is well known that he was a prudent and magnanimous man, and had it not been for that papal pestilence which at that time infected all peoples with its contagion, he would have deserved as well of the Church as of the commonwealth. William Lyndwood dedicated to this archbishop the archiepiscopal constitutions, which he had arranged by himself in a fine order and explained in most exact commentaries. William Lyndwood was first official of the Court of Arches, then keeper of the king's privy seal, and at last was raised to the see of St David's. This archbishop magnificently built, in the town of Higham Ferrers where (as we have said) he was born, a college, in which he placed secular clergy and prebendaries enriched with ecclesiastical benefices and dignities. And in the same town he founded a hospital for the poor, and acquired many estates for its use and for the alms of the poor; these, by his brothers Robert and William Chichele, citizens of London, whom he appointed his heirs in his will, were afterwards increased and enlarged, with very many other estates added and acquired. Nor was the archbishop content with these works, but at Oxford he founded, for the cultivation of letters, the most famous college of All Souls, and also St Bernard's College, which was afterwards enlarged by Thomas White, mayor of London, with the estates of a knight, and called St John's College. Moreover, at Canterbury he repaired the library and furnished it with books of every kind, built the greater part of the belfry, and gave the convent very many ornaments and jewels. While living, he built with the consent of the convent a tomb in Canterbury Cathedral, in which he was to be buried when dead. He first ordered that the proctors of his Court of Arches, when the judge was seated, should wear the dress which bachelors of arts use in the universities. In exercising jurisdiction he joined severity with equity, and he spared even those who had offended greatly. For Lord Strange and John Truffel, knight, being hostile to each other, met at the church of St Dunstan-in-the-East in London on Good Friday, and joined battle with their servants and retainers. In that fight and fray, when they had burst into the church, they killed Thomas Petwarden, a citizen of London of the same parish. Therefore the archbishop, the deed now done and Christian blood shed in the church, excommunicated all who had engaged in that fight and had rushed into the church. Afterwards he inquired into the first instigators of that constitution (of disturbance), and when he had learned that Lord Strange and his wife had given the first cause for so great a tumult, he ordered them to be named and proclaimed excommunicate by name at St Paul's Cross the following Sunday. They then came to him as suppliants on bended knees and begged with many entreaties to be absolved. The archbishop imposed on them this penance:

units.la: Vt proximo die dominico ille capite nudo, illaq; pedibus nudis ab Ecclesia Paulina ad Dunstani templum eum omnibus suis famulis atq; affectis qui pugnæ interfuerunt Ca& shy;misiis tantùmodo indutis per plateas publicè ineederent. Quos Reginaldus Kentwood Londinensis Archidiaconus ad concerandam illam sanguinis effusione polluiam Ec& shy;clesiam sequetetur. In consecratione autem peragenda domina Strange quæ mœstum suum ad eam pugnam mulieri vindicta instigauit, omnia vasa ad eam consecrationem necessaria aqua repleret. Tum Ecclesia iam consecrata, eaque huius violati templi ma& shy;ximè rea fuit, primo ornamentum aliquod decem libris æstimatum altari offerret, dein­de maritus eius D. Strange pixidem argenteum quinq; librarum templo dedicato do­naret. His gestis ad Ecclesiam Paulinam ad solutionem petituri eo quo priùs inceßê­runt modo, ad Archiepiscopum redirent.
units.tr: That on the next Sunday he, with his head and feet bare, should walk publicly through the streets from St Paul's Church to the church of St Dunstan, together with all his servants and those involved who had taken part in the fight, clothed only in shirts. Reginald Kentwood, Archdeacon of London, was to follow them to reconsecrate the church, which had been polluted by the shedding of blood. In performing the consecration, Lady Strange, who had goaded her husband into that fight out of a desire for revenge, was to fill all the vessels needed for the consecration with water. Then, once the church was consecrated, and since she was chiefly guilty of violating this temple, she was first to offer an ornament valued at ten pounds to the altar, and afterwards her husband, Master Strange, was to give a silver pyx worth five pounds to the dedicated temple. When these things had been done, they were to return to the Archbishop, going to St Paul's to seek absolution in the same manner as before.

units.la: Hoc tempore collegium Whittingtonense à Iohanne Couentre,& Iohanne Carpenter ciuibus Londinensibus hæredibus testamenti Richardi Whittington Londinienditum est. A quibus etiam noua porta Anglicè Newgat,quæ antea antri atque specus fœdissimi insitar fuit, ad hanc quâ hodie videmus speciem reducta & fabricata est. Demum Henricus Chicheley multis a se prudenter atque pie gestis postquàm, viginti nouem annis,ac uno mense sedisset tertio die mensis Maii hac vita functus est. Et in eo quem viuus extruxerat tumulo ad septentrionalem præsbyterii partem posito sepultus iacet.
units.tr: At this time Whittington College was sold by John Coventry and John Carpenter, citizens of London and heirs of the will of Richard Whittington. By them also the new gate, called Newgate in English, which had previously been like a very foul cave or den, was restored and rebuilt to the appearance we see today. Finally, Henry Chichele, after having done many things wisely and piously, died on the third day of May, having sat for twenty-nine years and one month. He lies buried in the tomb that he had built for himself while alive, placed on the north side of the chancel.

units.la: LXII. Iohannes Stafford.
units.tr: LXII. John Stafford.

units.la: Illustris iam familiæ atq; gentis præsul, post Henricus Chicheley vita functum Archiepiscopalem dignitatem suscepit, Celeberrimi Comitis Staffordiæ filius Abbatis Buriæ in Dorcestrēi comitatu natus est, strpemq; ac originem suam adolescens doctrinam nobilitauit. Profectus autem è lure consultorum scholis, in quibus doctoris gradu donatus est, in Arcuata curia forensium causarum aduocationi & patrocinio se dedit. Quem mox Henricus Chicheley Cantuariensis ante eum Archiepiscopus Vicarium suum in spiritualibus generalem,causarumq; ad Ecclesiasticum forum spectan- tium auditorem constituit. Atque his muneribus publicis adiecit Decanatum S. Martini Londini, & Præbendam Miltonensem in Ecclesia Cathedrali Lincoln. Iamq; Regi Henrico quinto cognitus intimis ac summis eius consiliis adhibitus priuati sigilli custodiam habuit. Tum thesaurarius Regni, & Wellensis Decanus,ac Canonicus Ecclesiæ cathedralis Sarisburiensis constitutus est, mortuoq; Henrico Rege quinto Bathoniensem Episcopatum à Martino quinto Papa prouisionis titulo accepit. Ac demum ad Ar- chiepiscopalem Celsitudinem ab Eugenio Papa à Bathoniensi Ecclesia translatus est. Nō dum enim illator legibus sanctionibusque vetita papalium prouisionum vsurpatio cessa- uit. Acceptis autem translationis suæ Bullis in xdibus Bathoniensis Episcopi ad Regem quitum Elthaniæ in Cantio fuit postridie properauit, redditoque ei fidei homagio tem- poralia Archiepiscopatus accepit. Tum crux à Iohanne Salisbury sacræ theologiæ pro- fessore & Priore Cauruariensi ibidem adducta,eiusque concepta solita verborum formula tradita est: Eodemq; etiam loco palliumab Eugenio Papa missum,ac ad se per Roffen- sem Episcopum delatum 23. Augusti induit. Iohannes Beckington primo in priuati sigilli custodia,deinde in Bathoniensi Episcopatu ei succeßit.
units.tr: This prelate, of an illustrious family and lineage, succeeded Henry Chicheley in the archiepiscopal dignity after his death. He was born the son of the most famous Earl of Stafford, of the Abbot of Bury in the county of Dorset. As a young man he ennobled his rank and descent by his learning. Having come from the schools of the lawyers, where he was made a doctor of laws, he devoted himself to the advocacy and patronage of cases in the Arches court. Archbishop Henry Chicheley, his predecessor at Canterbury, soon appointed him his general vicar in spiritual matters and auditor of causes belonging to the ecclesiastical court. To these public offices he added the deanery of St Martin's in London and the prebend of Milton in the cathedral church of Lincoln. Already known to King Henry V, he was admitted to his innermost and highest councils and held the custody of the privy seal. Then he was made treasurer of the realm, dean of Wells and canon of the cathedral church of Salisbury. When King Henry V died, he received the bishopric of Bath from Pope Martin V by the title of provision. Finally Pope Eugenius transferred him from the church of Bath to the archiepiscopal dignity. For the laws and sanctions had not yet put an end to the usurpation of papal provisions, which were forbidden. Having received the bulls of his translation in the house of the bishop of Bath, he hastened the next day to the king at Eltham in Kent, and after he had rendered the oath of fealty to him, he received the temporalities of the archbishopric. Then the cross was brought there by John Salisbury, professor of sacred theology and prior of Canterbury, and handed to him with the customary form of words. In the same place he put on the pallium sent by Pope Eugenius and brought to him by the bishop of Rochester, on 23 August. John Beckington succeeded him first in the custody of the privy seal, and then in the bishopric of Bath.

units.la: Hocanno Henricus sexrus Angliæ Rex summus bonarū literarum patronus duo Re- galia literarum studiis consecrata collegia inchoauit. Vnum Etoniæ quod prope arcem Windesorinam in qua Rex natus est,positum est. Alterum Cantebrigiæ. Itaq; Elienfi- Episcopo mortuo in cuius diocæsis Cantabrigia sita est, Iohannes Stratford Archiepisco- pus Lincolniensis atque Sarisburiensi Episcopis mense Ianuario mandauit,vt Cæmiteri- um, Altare, & Campanas illius incepti Collegii consecrarent. Secundo translationis suæ anno Regeprescipiente synodum Londini celebrauit. In ea cum de subsidio Regi tribu- endo ageretur,Clerus periit vi statuta prouisionum, & breuia seu actiones de Præmuni- re quæ callida & malitiosa leguleiorum interpretatione ad Cleri pernicie & Ecclesiasticæ disciplinæ turbatione conuersa sunt, aut penitus abrogentur aut humaniori ac benigniori iure nitantur. Deinde vt eodem modo de grossis atboribus non decimandis æquius statuatur. Postremò vt contra laicos qui Clericos in Regiis foris falso & iniuste exagirant, grauis aliqua pœna sanciatur. Verum concessa Regi decima, de his Cleri postulatis sy- nodus vlterius deliberandum censuit,atque discessit. Eodem anno Archiepiscopus per totam prouinciam Cantuariensem edixit, vt Nundinæ & Emporia in Ecclesiis aut cæ- miteriis, diebusque dominicis atque festis præterquam tempore messis non tenentur.
units.tr: In this year Henry VI, king of England and the greatest patron of good letters, began two royal colleges devoted to the study of letters. One was at Eton, which lies near the castle of Windsor where the king was born. The other was at Cambridge. Therefore, when the bishop of Ely, in whose diocese Cambridge lies, had died, Archbishop John Stratford, bishop of Lincoln and Salisbury, in January ordered that the cemetery, altar and bells of that new college be consecrated. In the second year of his translation he held a synod at London at the king's command. In it, when the granting of a subsidy to the king was under discussion, the clergy petitioned that the statutes of provisors and the writs or actions of praemunire, which by the crafty and malicious interpretation of the lawyers had been turned to the destruction of the clergy and the disturbance of ecclesiastical discipline, be either entirely repealed or rest upon a more humane and kindly law. Next, that in the same way it be more fairly enacted about great tithes which are not to be tithed. Last, that some heavy penalty be decreed against laymen who falsely and unjustly drag clergymen before the royal courts. But when a tenth had been granted to the king, the synod judged that these requests of the clergy should be considered further, and it broke up. In the same year the archbishop issued an edict throughout the province of Canterbury that markets and fairs were not to be held in churches or cemeteries, nor on Sundays and feast days, except at harvest time.

units.la: Ac proximo anno Arch. Margaretam Reginam Henrico Regi Westmon. penultimo die mensis Maii nuptiis coniunxit, eamq; cōsecrauit. Iamq; iuris regni peritî vt qui commodi causa Regia fora multitudine litium & infinitate replerent,pleraq; causas & con- trouersias ab Archiepiscopali & Episcopali audientia ad sua iudicia vocabant, & Ecclesiasticam iurisdictionem declinarum, matrimoniorum, & testamentorum atq; vltimarum voluntatum finibus & cæcellis concludere volebant,in quibus etiam sæpe eius pu- testatem prohibitionibus Regis coercebant & impediebant. Tum illa prouisionum sta- ruta tuta, & breuia de Præmunire, si prælati ac iudices Ecclesiastici, digitū (vt aiunt) latū præscriptos a se iurisdictionis fines transfulerent, multus minus vibrabant. Ea poena prælatis valde terribilis fuit. Nam si laicis iudicibus rei pronunciarentur, & bonis omnibus mulctandi, & æternis carcerum tenebris inuoluendi erant. Huius poenæ atrocitatem Episcopi & Prælati iurisdictione præditi ita perplexi & perturbati sunt, vt quia Legulejorum minantia tela vix vitare poterant, concilium fine mora in eundem putarunt, & Londini synodo conuenerunt. In ea supplicationem totius AnglicaniClerino mine conceptam Regi tradiderunt, in qua de laicis iudicibus oppido semperque Clericis infestis grauiter conquesti sunt. Nullam esse causam dixerunt cur pro Regis, regniq; incolumitate ac salute maior fides consuetudinum quam legum peritis sibique Ecclesiasticæ iurisdictionis prælatis haberetur. Se enim iure certo hærere ac insistere, illos arbitrio vagari, & iura pro causis quotidiana suo æri insculpere, eademq; in causis eisdem figere, tollere, ac refigere. Tum quod in aliis statutis si Parliamenti authoritate edantur (quo quidem iure nescitur) interpretationem sibi peculiariter arrogare, & leges, condentium intentiones atq; mentes (quæ sola lex omnibus humanis legibus imperitat) incertis, motiuis & decretis impudenter & imperiose quocunque vellent deducere. Non esse autem aliam Regi causam cur prælatorum fides sibi in dubiū veniret, quàm quod proribus fœculis Clerus a Rege defecit, & Romano Pontifici adhæsit. Nunc autē eadē ista lata iura q prælatis ipsis in Parlamento contra Romanū pontificē deprecantibus proiure Regio sanctita sunt in prælatos, regni iniqua Iuridicorū & Leguleiorū calumniacensuraq; torqueri. Id quod ex vno inani verbo ab aliquo litigioso calumniatore perperā interpretato perspicit facile posset. Nam Lex his defertis verbis lancita est: Ethat if any purchase or purse fue / or do to be purchased or pursued in the Court of Rome or else where, any such translations ons/Processes, and sentences of excommunications/Bulles/instruments/ or any other things, which touch the Kingʃ against him/ his Regalie/ or his Realme. &c. Si quis impetret aut persequatur, te impetrari vel persequi procuret in curia Romana seu alibi, aliquas eiusmodi translationes, Processus, & sententias excommunicationum, Bullas, instrumenta, vel aliam rem quamcunq; quæ Regem tangat, contra eum, eius regalem dignitatem, vel regnum. Ex his verbis Caudici qui Prælatos sanctionum periculis inuoluere velle nec, cauillantur hac tam grauiter poena Ecclesiasticos iudices teneri si quantulumcunq; in iurisdictionem Regiam commisetit, aut quouis modo tirubauerint. Quo terrore propositio perdifficilis & periculosa erat Ecclesiasticæ iurisdictionis tam arctis coercitæ finibus tractatio. Quod eo est iniquius quia statutum illud in prælatorū gratiam latum est. Cum enim indignissimi antea quiq; ad Papam promiscuē confugissent, ab eoq; nummis interuenientibus opulentissimē beneficia & maximas dignitates Ecclesiasticas impetrassent, nec prælati ea ambitione & cupiditate Romana impediti Ecclesias quarum essent patroni, liberē conferre poterant, proscriptione sanctum est: Ne Regis deinceps subdi Ecclesiarum prouisiones à Papa peterent, aut citationes, processus, excommunicationes, vel Ecclesiasticas censuras à Papa Romæ seu alibi ratione huiusmodi prouisionum decretas interpositas aut fulminatas, in Anglia vel alibi contra Regem aut Regis subditos exequetentur, denunciaret, aut promulgaret. Quod verbum alibi calumniosi legulei malitiosa interpretatione conuertunt in prælatos, eiusque sensum esse callide fingunt, si de causa ciuili non modo Romæ sed in Ecclesiasticis foris & consistoriis quæ curias Christianitatis appellant, etiam in regno, lis forte interueniat. At lege alium fuisse illorum sensum quorum consensu conditum tum statutum fuit certum est, qui illud verbū in curia Romana, vel alibi interposuerunt. Quia Papaipse sæpe ab urbe Romana Lugduni, Pisis, Auinione, aliisq; locis Roma longe latèq; disiunctis abfuit, in quibus illa ptouisionum iura non minus quàm Romæ vsurpauit. Tū legatos Papæ eadem ipso Papæ nomine frequenter facere, quibus perinde illa salubertis mafanctione occurrendum fuit, quàm his quæ Romæ fiunt. Itaq; contra omnem iuris & æquitatis rationem esse, vt quæ salubriter in Prælatorum vtilitatem constituta sunt, tiniquissimis interpretantium cauillis in eorum perniciem torqueantur. Præterea quis existimare queat tam insanos tum fuisse Episcopos vt tam duris & sæuis si modo lta accipiantur in se legibus vellent consentire? Nam si causas forte ciuiles in suis foris tractent, pedemq; in Regis iurisdictionem intulerint, an eadem poena afficiendi censeretur qua Papæ prouisores? Etenim omni eq̃uo & rationabilli iure, pœnam conuenit esse delicto parem. Itaque si iurisdictionis finibus commisse fines exeant, non nisi ipso iure tam graues pœnas ineurraut, sed prohibitionibus coerceantur.
units.tr: In the following year the archbishop joined Queen Margaret to King Henry at Westminster on the penultimate day of May, and consecrated her. Now the lawyers, skilled in the law of the realm, who filled the royal courts with a multitude and infinity of lawsuits for their own profit, were summoning most cases and disputes from the archiepiscopal and episcopal courts to their own tribunals. They were declining ecclesiastical jurisdiction and wanted to confine the causes of marriages, wills and last wills within narrow limits, and in these matters they often hindered and checked the archbishop's power by the king's prohibitions. Then those statutes of provisors and the writs of praemunire, if prelates and ecclesiastical judges moved (as they say) a finger's breadth beyond the boundaries of jurisdiction prescribed to them, brandished them much more. That penalty was very terrifying to the prelates. For if they were condemned as guilty by lay judges, they were to be stripped of all their goods and shut up in the eternal darkness of prisons. The bishops and prelates endowed with jurisdiction were so bewildered and disturbed by the severity of this penalty that, since they could scarcely avoid the threatening weapons of the lawyers, they thought a council should be held without delay against it, and they assembled at London in a synod. In it they handed to the king a supplication drawn up in the name of the whole English clergy, in which they complained gravely that laymen as judges were very hostile and always unfriendly to clergymen. They said there was no reason why greater trust should be placed in the customs of men skilled in the laws than in the prelates of ecclesiastical jurisdiction, who were concerned with the safety and welfare of the king and the realm. For they, they said, adhered to and kept to a fixed law, whereas the others wandered at their own whim, and carved laws daily into their bronze to suit each case, and fixed them, removed them and fixed them again in the same cases. Then, too, in other statutes enacted by the authority of Parliament (by what right is not known), the lawyers shamelessly and arrogantly claimed for themselves a special power of interpretation, and wanted to lead wherever they pleased the intentions and minds of the lawmakers (which alone is the law that governs all human laws) by uncertain motives and decrees. The reason the king had for doubting the good faith of the prelates, they said, was not other than that in former ages the clergy had revolted from the king and clung to the Roman pontiff. But now those same laws, passed by royal authority against the prelates themselves when they had protested in Parliament against the Roman pontiff, were being turned by the lawyers' and jurists' unjust calumnies and censures against the prelates and the realm. This could easily be seen from a single empty word wrongly interpreted by some quarrelsome slanderer. For the law is enacted in these words: "And that if any purchase or pursue, or do to be purchased or pursued, in the Court of Rome or elsewhere, any such translations, processes and sentences of excommunications, bulls, instruments or any other thing which touches the King, against him, his regality or his realm, etc." The English words, as quoted, are: "And that if any purchase or purse fue, or do to be purchased or pursued in the Court of Rome or else where, any such translations, processes, and sentences of excommunications, bulles, instruments, or any other things, which touch the King, against him, his Regalie, or his Realme. &c." The Latin rendering is: if anyone procures or pursues, or causes to be procured or pursued, in the Roman court or elsewhere, any such translations, processes and sentences of excommunication, bulls, instruments, or any other thing whatsoever which touches the king, against him, his royal dignity or the realm. From these words the sophists who want to entangle the prelates in the dangers of the statutes argue that ecclesiastical judges are bound by so grave a penalty if they have committed the slightest offence against royal jurisdiction, or have in any way disturbed it. By this terror it was a most difficult and perilous matter to treat ecclesiastical jurisdiction, so tightly confined within its limits. This was the more unjust because that statute was enacted for the favour of the prelates. For since in former times the most unworthy men had freely resorted to the pope, and from him, with money intervening, had obtained the most opulent benefices and the greatest ecclesiastical dignities, and since the prelates, hindered by that Roman ambition and greed, could not freely confer the churches of which they were patrons, it was enacted by prohibition that the king's subjects should no longer seek provisions of churches from the pope, nor should any citations, processes, excommunications or ecclesiastical censures decreed or issued at Rome or elsewhere by the pope on account of such provisions be enforced or proclaimed or promulgated in England or elsewhere against the king or the king's subjects. The lawyers, bent on slander, twist the word "elsewhere" by malicious interpretation against the prelates, and craftily pretend that its meaning is that if a civil cause arises, not only at Rome but in ecclesiastical courts and consistories, which they call courts of Christendom, even within the realm, the statute applies. But it is certain that the meaning of those who agreed to enact that statute, and of those who inserted the words "in the Roman court or elsewhere", was different. For the pope himself was often absent from the city of Rome, at Lyon, Pisa, Avignon and other places far and wide apart from Rome, where he claimed those rights of provision no less than at Rome. Then the pope's legates often made provisions in the pope's own name, and these had to be met by that salutary sanction just as much as those made at Rome. Therefore it is against every principle of law and equity that things established for the salutary advantage of the prelates should be twisted to their ruin by the most unjust quibbles of interpreters. Moreover, who could think the bishops of that time were so mad that they would wish to consent to laws so harsh and cruel, if they were taken in this sense? For if they handled civil causes in their own courts, and set foot in the king's jurisdiction, would they be judged liable to the same penalty as the papal provisors? For by every fair and reasonable law, it is fitting that the penalty be equal to the offence. Therefore, if they overstep the boundaries of their jurisdiction, they incur not such grave penalties by the law itself, but are checked by prohibitions.

units.la: Quas si contempserint vindicentur de contemptu: Legum enim poenas verborum ambiguitate ad causas non expressas nulloiure referendas, sed si verborum vlum in condendalege ambiguû interueniat, etiamsi de contendentium mente nô appareat, tamen id in benigniorem significationem interpretatione deducendum. Ad extremum addiderunt, iniquè secun agi quòd laicorum iudicum, qui vt Ecclesiastica iurisdictio penitus eneruetur, & contemptui vulgo fiat quidlibet statuere vellent tanquam inimicorum censuras & iudicia patiantur. Summa petitionis huius fuit, vt Parlamenti interpretatione illa vox alibi quæ tam perplexam difficultatem induxit declaretur, tam vt Ecclesiastici iudices nisi prohibitiones Regias spreuerint illa tam atroci contra prouisores poenanon teneantur: postremò vt hi qui de iuridictionis finibus totis viribus contra praelatos tam hostiliter semper dimicare solent à concedendis prohibitionibus, & cognoscendis huiusmodi causis, exercendiq; iu Ecclesiasticos iudices iudiciis supersedeant. Aliud statuentur, qui cum de iurisdictionis vtriusque finibus agatur, aut illæ causæ in controuersiam veniunt, fineomni suspicione & interpretari controuersia iura aequius, & sine invidia iudicare rectius velint. In hac autem re Polidorus Virgilius falsus est.
units.tr: If they despise these, let them be punished for contempt. For the penalties of the laws cannot be extended by any right to cases the words do not express. But if the usage of the words in framing a law is ambiguous, then even where the intention of the parties does not appear, the matter must be interpreted in the milder sense. Finally, they added that it was unjust for them to be treated in this way, that the lay judges, so that ecclesiastical jurisdiction might be wholly weakened and made contemptible among the common people, wished to decree whatever they liked, and that they should suffer the censures and judgments of enemies. The sum of this petition was that the meaning of that phrase elsewhere, which has caused such a perplexing difficulty, be declared by Parliament, and that ecclesiastical judges not be liable to that savage penalty against the provisors unless they have disregarded the royal prohibitions. Last, they asked that those who have always fought so hostilely against the prelates with all their strength over the limits of jurisdiction should refrain from granting prohibitions, from hearing cases of this kind, and from exercising judgments against the ecclesiastical judges. Others would decree, when the limits of both jurisdictions are in dispute and such cases come into controversy, that the laws be interpreted more fairly and judged more rightly, free of all suspicion and of ill will. In this matter, however, Polydore Virgil is mistaken.

units.la: Quod Martinus Papam qui diu ante obiit cum Henrico sexto Rege de rescindendis illis iuribus & actionibus eguisse, & illa statuta quæ contra Papæ prouisiones lata sunt à poenis prouisis & praemonitis nunc quoque incarit esse scribat. Sed vt omisso homine peregrino & à nostræ historiæ sensu veritateq; alieno ad hanc praesulum atq; praelatorum supplicationem reueretur. Situm cum Papa authoritatem Regiam in omni iurisdictione exercebat. Cùm vis eius etiam Regibus esset formidabilis, tamen contra tam immanem & violentam iuris regni peritorum interpretationem deprecari Praelati coacti sunt, quid nunc facient cum Ecclesiasticæ iurisdictionis gubernaculis Principi delatis, & papali vsurpatione exclusa, nec illa Causidicorum turba, neq; quisquâ institutus hominum ordo maiote fide, religione, doctrina, prudentia, & facundia papalem oppugnent & Principis iurisdictionem ruentur quàm Praelati. Vt grauiori supplicio digni sunt hi, qui Ecclesiastica iudicia iam contra Papam, eaquè Principis nomine exercitata, obsoletis illorum statutorum calumniis nunc impediant, & praelatos à munere suo pie recteq; gerendo deterreant quàm qui prisci illis tempotibus papales prouisiones Romæ vel alibi impetrarent.
units.tr: He writes that Pope Martin, who died long before, had sought with King Henry VI the rescinding of those rights and actions, and that those statutes passed against papal provisions still carry the penalties provided and forewarned. But, leaving aside this foreigner, who is alien to the sense and truth of our history, let me return to this petition of the bishops and prelates. When the Pope exercised royal authority in every jurisdiction, and his power was feared even by kings, the prelates were nevertheless compelled to protest against so monstrous and violent an interpretation of the laws of the kingdom by its lawyers. What will they now do, when the helm of ecclesiastical jurisdiction has been handed to the Prince and the papal usurpation has been shut out? Neither that crowd of pleaders, nor any other order of men, will attack the papal power and defend the Prince's jurisdiction with more loyalty, piety, learning, prudence and eloquence than the prelates. Those deserve a heavier punishment who now, by the stale slanders of those old statutes, hinder the ecclesiastical courts that are now exercised against the Pope in the Prince's name, and deter the prelates from discharging their office piously and rightly, than those who in those former times obtained papal provisions at Rome or elsewhere.

units.la: Quod si tam iniqui calumniatores duriores esse volunt, & vetera ob alias causas lata iura non ad Principis aut Reip. sed ad sua vtilitatem atque quæstū, & ad integerrimi religiosissimiq; praelatorum ordinis perniciem refricare volunt, saltem ipsi simili lege lata patianturlegem talionis: eademque poena plectantur si in Ecclesiasticæ iuridictionis limites incurrant, qua praelatos, si suas causas vel minimo digito attingerent, affici volunt. Nunc reliquam huius Archiepiscopi historiam quæ perbreuis est, absoluamus. Hoc ipso anno quo haec acta sunt, Eugenius Papa qui maiorum suorum exemplo fel cum melle permiscuit, ad Henricum Regem sextum aureum Rosam instituta solenni legatione misit, & literis scriptis de eius natura ac virtute, tum quibus ceremoniis Romæ quotannis in Ecclesia S. Petri celebratur, multa declarauit.
units.tr: But if such unjust slanderers wish their own position to be harsher, and wish to revive old laws, passed for other reasons, not for the good of the Prince or the commonwealth but for their own profit and gain, and to the ruin of the most upright and religious order of prelates, let them at least submit to a law of the same kind, the law of retaliation, and let them be punished with the same penalty they wish to inflict on the prelates, if they should trespass on the limits of ecclesiastical jurisdiction. Now let us finish the rest of this Archbishop's history, which is very brief. In this same year in which these things were done, Pope Eugenius, who after the example of his predecessors mingled gall with honey, sent to King Henry VI the Golden Rose by a solemn legation, and in a letter declared much about its nature and virtue, and about the ceremonies by which it is celebrated every year at Rome in the Church of St Peter.

units.la: Hanc aureum Rosam Lodouicus quidam S. Stephani Westmonasterii Archiepiscopo Cant. tum Regni Cancellario, & Archiepiscopo Eboracensi Iohanne Kemp Cardinali, nec non Eboracensi & Exoniensi Ducibus praesentibus obtulit. Quem Papæ benignitatem Rex non modò rescriptis gratiis sed plurimis donis remuneravit. Verùm Papa cum Regem tam inani muinsculo permulsum & delenitum existimasset, manum admouit grauioribus. Exegit ab Anglicano Clero omnium prouentuum decimas, ad easquè colligendas nuncios cum Bullis ad Archiepiscopum Canruarien sem destinauit. Sed Rex comperta tam recondita fraude Archiepiscopû veruit no obsequeretur Papæ. Itaque Archiepiscopus literis se ad Papam de suis mandatis Regio iussu peragi interdictus excusauit, eiusquè nuncios spe ac expectatione inani deceptos remisit Romam.
units.tr: Lewis, a certain man of St Stephen's, Westminster, presented this Golden Rose in the presence of the Archbishop of Canterbury, then Chancellor of the kingdom, of John Kemp, Archbishop of York and Cardinal, and of the Dukes of York and Exeter. The King rewarded the Pope's kindness not only with gracious letters but with many gifts. But when the Pope thought the King had been soothed and mollified by so empty a little gift, he laid his hand on heavier matters. He demanded from the English clergy the tithes of all their revenues, and to collect them he sent messengers with bulls to the Archbishop of Canterbury. But the King, having discovered so hidden a fraud, forbade the Archbishop to obey the Pope. Accordingly the Archbishop excused himself by letter to the Pope, saying that he had been forbidden by the King's order to carry out his commands, and he sent the Pope's messengers back to Rome, deceived in their vain hope and expectation.

units.la: Toto huius Archiepiscopi tempore Papa prouisione adhuc Episcopos statuit.
